exact_request.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one original category artwork for Ben Ebsworth's Blog/Lab research folio; a proposed artwork study, not an approved topic.
Style and medium: a sophisticated hand-drawn graphite engraving of a tactile miniature object, warm ivory material, fine charcoal contours, selective crosshatching and etched grain. Quiet authored editorial character, not a generic icon or glossy 3D product tile.
Composition and framing: square canvas, the entire single subject centred within the middle 64 percent of the canvas. Keep at least 18 percent genuinely empty margin on every edge. A clear, distinctive silhouette with meaningful internal negative space; coherent three-quarter view. All parts fully inside the frame.
Colour and material: graphite black, charcoal grey and warm ivory only, with one small restrained vermilion red material detail occupying less than five percent of the subject. The red detail is part of the object, not a label, glow or operational status.
Background and lighting: genuinely transparent alpha outside the object and through its open spaces. Solid opaque subject surfaces with natural antialiased silhouette edges. No backdrop, no paper rectangle, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no outer glow, no halo, no luminous edge or coloured fringe. Shading is contained within the object.
Constraints: create only this one original subject. No text, no letters, no numbers, no tick labels, no equations, no fake inscriptions, no arrows or annotation lines, no readable code, no watermark, no logo, no badge border. This is an illustrative metaphor, not a scientifically accurate diagram, measurement, real dataset, model output or functioning apparatus.
Subject: A compact branching chance mechanism: a single upper feed chute divides into two substantial Y-shaped grooved channels, then into four open terminal cups, forming a sculptural branching silhouette. Small ivory balls are held at different forks; one small red ball rests at the first decision fork. Mechanical dividers and channel lips are clearly drawn. The physical forks, empty gaps and four outcomes are the visual idea; avoid a generic node-link graph and avoid dice, playing cards or percentages.
